claims.text: Spark plasma sintering can promote a large-scale in situ reaction between RHEAs and Cu.
Spark plasma sintering rapidly densifies the RHEA/Cu material.
Spark plasma sintering kinetically limits phase segregation caused by positive heat of mixing.
The starting material consists of separate RHEA and Cu powders.
There is a positive heat of mixing between the refractory alloying elements and Cu.
The proposed intervention is SPS under controlled temperature, pressure, and dwell time.
High heating rates, moderate-to-high pressure, and short sintering times permit rapid diffusion and reaction.
Short sintering times minimize the prolonged diffusion that could drive phase separation.
SPS forms a finely dispersed interfacial region between the RHEA and Cu phases.
Transient metastable phases may contribute to stabilization of the composite microstructure.
Rapid heating and applied pressure accelerate interfacial diffusion and reaction during SPS.
SPS overcomes the mixing-enthalpy challenge by kinetically trapping the composite microstructure before equilibrium phase separation.
SPS produces a dense RHEA/Cu composite.
Cu remains well dispersed within the refractory matrix after SPS.
The SPS-processed composite exhibits enhanced mechanical strength.
The SPS-processed composite exhibits enhanced thermal stability.
Conventional sintering generally provides excessive diffusion time and consequently promotes segregation in RHEA/Cu composites.
The proposed effect may fail when heating rate, pressure, and holding time are not optimized.
Production scale can alter heat flow and reaction kinetics, potentially preventing the proposed effect.
Quantitative relationships between SPS parameters, reaction kinetics, and microstructural stability have not been established in the hypothesis.
